qualification: Pre-fix mp4_audio_index, mp4_aac_index, matroska_audio_index, and matroska_aac_index in src/native_media.rs ignored Mp4Reader::automatic_track_indices and WebmReader::preferred_track_numbers when selected.is_none(), rejecting multi-audio MP4 and Matroska files with a single enabled movie/default audio track, and export_pcm_selected in src/native_export.rs omitted in-band PS negotiation so implicit-PS AAC streams exported with channels=1 and doubled sample_frames (19,200 instead of 9,600). Pre-fix baseline reproduced all defects and the forced acceptance test failed.

Updating src/native_media.rs and src/native_export.rs selects the sole enabled/preferred audio track when selected.is_none(), preserves explicit stream selection and ambiguous multi-enabled refusal, and negotiates in-band PS before configuring the export PCM pipeline and WAV header.

All 3 synthetic MP4 controls (disabled-first AAC, enabled-nonmovie-first AAC, disabled-first sowt PCM), remuxed Matroska dual-audio controls, existing audiovisual fixtures, and implicit-PS WAV export match analytical float32 PCM within 1e-6 and exact stereo WAV geometry (48,000 Hz, 2 channels, 9,600 frames).
2 focused tests, 25 related MP4/Matroska/PS integration tests, 14 MP4 unit tests, 359 minimal-configuration (--no-default-features) tests, offline fixture unittest, and full player build pass.

ISO/IEC 14496-12:2015, 8.3.2 (tkhd flags), RFC 9559 (Matroska FlagEnabled/FlagDefault), and ISO/IEC 14496-3:2009 (implicit PS signalling) govern automatic track selection and stereo output negotiation. All fixtures are pure synthetic offline files requiring neither FFmpeg nor network access.
counting: One automatic audio track selection and in-band PS export geometry alignment fix across src/native_media.rs and src/native_export.rs (FVID-0188). No extra IDs for individual fixture variants or controls.
